summary: @servicetitan/marketing-form preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute a bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall script (`node setup.mjs`, declared in package.json) unconditionally downloads a Bun runtime binary from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases at install time, chmod +x's it in a temp directory, and uses it to execute a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated JavaScript blob using hex-mangled identifiers (`_0x...`), a rotated string/opcode array (`n7gIxM=[...]` shuffled via `MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift())`), and a custom `fromCodePoint`-based string decoder — a shape that defeats Node-based inspection. The preinstall additionally fingerprints the host libc by invoking `ldd --version` and reading `/etc/os-release` to select between `bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline` and `bun-linux-x64-baseline`, ensuring the payload can execute across Linux libc variants. The advertised purpose is a React marketing-form helper, which has no legitimate need for a second language runtime or an opaque multi-hundred-KB install-time payload. The package name uses the `@servicetitan` scope, which does not correspond to a verified publisher for this artifact. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: a second runtime is fetched specifically to execute obfuscated attacker-shipped code on the installer's machine as a side effect of `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
